IncidentsBot: [ALERT] Spike in 5xxs on /v1/generate (error rate +8% over 5m). Queue depth increasing on production-runtime-1. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/alerts/5xx-spike :rotating_light:
Alex: ack. I'm oncall. Triage starting — can someone grab recent runtime logs and look for KV/cache thrashing? @Maya can you take lead?
Maya: looking now. Initial grep shows a lot of KV cache misses and repeated model reloads on a subset of hosts (gpu-pool-b). Host mem pressure + CPU spikes. Rolling GC chatter in logs. Scaling actions: will spin up 2 extra nodes from reserved pool and enable burst_capacity.
Alex: good. While Maya scales, we need fast live mitigations to protect customer experience. Proposal: 1) apply soft per-api-key rate limit (10 rps) for public tier; 2) set default max_tokens to 512 for non-enterprise keys; 3) enable model fallback to quantized-1 where available. Anyone object?
Jin: +1 for fallback. Will flip feature flag fallback_quant_v1 -> true for the affected region. Also enabling soft-queue enforcement so long-running queued requests are rejected early with 429 instead of timing out.
Sam: for SDKs/devs: we should push quick client guidance now. Recommend immediate client-side changes: - exponential backoff with capped jitter, start at 250ms, factor 2, max 5 retries; - treat 429/503/504 as retryable; - require idempotency: include request_id header for any non-idempotent operations and *do not* retry without it; - for streams switch to resume tokens if available. I'll paste suggested snippet for JS/Node below.
Sam: ```js
// SDK guidance: simple retry interceptor
const RETRIES = 5
const BASE = 250 // ms
function sleep(ms){ return new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, ms)) }
axios.interceptors.response.use(null, async (err) => {
  const status = err.response ? err.response.status : null
  if (!err.config || err.config.__retried >= RETRIES) return Promise.reject(err)
  if (![429, 503, 504].includes(status)) return Promise.reject(err)
  err.config.__retried = (err.config.__retried || 0) + 1
  const backoff = BASE * Math.pow(2, err.config.__retried - 1)
  const jitter = Math.random() * 100
  await sleep(backoff + jitter)
  return axios(err.config)
})
// Also: set a request_id header: headers['x-request-id'] = uuidv4()
```
Maya: thanks — I'll add a note on the runtime side to return Retry-After where appropriate and include machine-readable error body for the SDK to detect transient failures.
Priya: prepping status update: "Some customers may see elevated errors or longer response times. We have applied traffic shaping and are rolling fallbacks. We'll post further updates in 30m." I can ping impacted customers directly if you list them.
Alex: list of currently impacted customer IDs in the dashboard filter. Priya please send a templated note and include mitigation steps + ETA.
Jin: runtime change applied: fallback_quant_v1 = true (region us-west). Dropping low-priority background inference jobs and enabling soft-queue enforcement now. Observability: queue length down ~40% after node add.
Sam: small addition for streaming clients — recommend that SDKs default to a 10s inactivity heartbeat and, on stream error, attempt resume with resume_token if server returns one. If not available, surface partial result and guide devs to re-request with request_id to avoid double-processing. Also recommend jitter on the first backoff (random 0-100ms) to avoid thundering herd.
Alex: temporary quota action: for a handful of strategic partners we may issue a short-term quota increase to keep SLA customers unaffected. Requesting signoff from @DeployBot or @Jin for capacity constraints.
DeployBot: auto-approval criteria check: small, time-limited quota increases (<= 2x for <= 2 hours) allowed if capacity headroom > 10%. Current headroom after scale: ~12% — proceeding with manual increases for listed partners.
Priya: customer communications drafted; will post to status and send targeted emails. Include rollback criteria: we will revert rate limits and model fallbacks once 5xx rate is below 1% for 15m sustained. Timeline: monitoring for next 120 minutes.
Alex: agree on rollback criteria. On-call handoff: my shift ends in 25m — Maya, you'll take over monitoring and incident lead if anything regresses. I'll stay reachable for escalation.
Maya: ack, taking over. I'll keep the postmortem skeleton updated with timeline and decisions (rate limits, model fallback, SDK guidance).
Sam: I'll cut a small patch to SDK docs and publish a hotfix that surfaces retry policy guidance in the next 30m. Will add snippet to changelog and an inline deprecation notice for any older retry behavior.
Alex: summary for handoff -> root cause still under investigation (cache misses + node mem pressure causing model reloads). Mitigations in place: +2 nodes, soft per-key 10rps limit, default max_tokens 512 for public, fallback to quantized model, soft-queue enforcement, client SDK retry/backoff guidance published. Monitoring: dashboards + alert thresholds adjusted.
Priya: posted status page and emailed 6 customers flagged as impacted.
Jin: monitoring: error rate trending down but still elevated ~2.8%. Keeping fallback enabled; will revert in 2hr if stable.
Alex: thanks team. If you see any sustained regression ping me and I'll re-open paging. Handing off to Maya now. :handshake:
Maya: will follow up with a concise incident blurb for postmortem. tagging: @Sam for SDK note, @Priya for comms, @Jin for runtime changes.
IncidentsBot: Incident marked acknowledged by Alex. Timeline note created.
<reactions> :thumbsup::eyes:
